ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r8.speaker: مجاهد، عبيد بن عمير، ابن محيصن، يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r8.claim: The majority read “we do not establish a weight” with first-person plural and accusative wazana; other readings use third-person singular or intransitive yaqumu, with wazan as its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فلا نقيم بالنون وزنا بالنصب ومجاهد وعبيد بن عمير فلا يقيم بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r9.claim: Not establishing a weight may mean the losers have no good deeds to weigh and therefore enter the Fire, or figuratively that they have no worth with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r9.anchor: واحتمل قوله فلا نقيم إلا به أنهم لا حسنة لهم توزن في موازين القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r10.claim: Two reports illustrate the verse: a glutton, drinker, and tall man will not weigh even a mosquito's wing; other people bring deeds as large as Tihama mountains that weigh nothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r10.anchor: يؤتى بالأكول الشروب الطويل فلا يزن جناح بعوضة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.claim: An objection says the next verse calls them unbelievers, unlike Kharijites who do not deny resurrection; the answer is that مِن can mean sharing only their misguidance, or ʿAli may have judged them unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.anchor: وأجيب بأن من اتصالية فلا يلزم أن يكونوا متصلين بهم من كل الوجوه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.claim: Their deeds are canceled and they have no value or standing on Resurrection Day; Arabs say a person has no weight to mean no worth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.anchor: أي لا نجعل لهم خطرا وقدرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a large, heavy man will weigh no more than a gnat's wing with God, and the Prophet cited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "ليأتي الرجل العظيم السمين يوم القيامة لا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.claim: He says some people bring deeds they considered as large as the mountains of Tihāma, yet those deeds weigh nothing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخدري: يأتي أناس بأعمال يوم القيامة هي عندهم في العظم كجبال تهامة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r7.claim: Their efforts fail because they disbelieve in God’s signs and meeting Him, leaving nothing to restrain their desires.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r7.anchor: فصاروا لا يخافون فلا يردهم شيء عن أهوائهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r8.claim: Their good deeds are null because they lack faith as their foundation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r8.anchor: أي سقطت وبطلت وفسدت بسبب جحدهم للدلائل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r9.claim: God assigns them no weight on Judgment Day: no one can object to His majesty or intercede without His leave, and they ignored His signs and felt secure from His scheme.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r9.anchor: ما لنا من الكبرياء والعظمة المانعين

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r4.claim: The Prophet says that a huge, heavy person may weigh no more than a gnat's wing before God, citing the verse that says they will have no weight on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إنه ليأتي الرجل العظيم السمين يوم القيامة لا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.claim: Heavy scales figuratively signal God's approval through abundant good deeds; Arabic uses weight for merit and honor, so the deeds need not be named explicitly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.anchor: وثقل الموازين كناية عن كونه بمحل الرضى من الله تعالى لكثرة حسناته

JISHUMI:v6p4501/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r2.claim: Resurrection gathers creation to reward and punish them; warning people of this benefits those held morally responsible.
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r2.anchor: إثبات المعاد وأنه يجمع بين الخلق ليثيب المثاب ويعاقب المعاقب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r8.claim: They may lack weight because their sins make them contemptible before God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r8.anchor: لهوانهم على الله تعالى بمعاصيهم التي ارتكبوها يصيرون محقورين

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r9.claim: Ignorance and folly make them light as though weightless.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r9.anchor: لخفتهم بالجهل وطيشهم بالسفه صاروا كمن لا وزن لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r10.claim: Their sins may erase their weight until nothing balances them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r10.anchor: أن المعاصي تذهب بوزنهم حتى لا يوازنوا من خفتهم شيئا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r11.claim: Unbelief nullifies their good deeds, leaving only evil deeds weighed against them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r11.anchor: أن حسناتهم تحبط بالكفر فتبقى سيئاتهم . فيكون الوزن عليهم لا لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r12.speaker: كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r12.claim: A man may weigh less than a grain or a gnat's wing on Resurrection Day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r12.anchor: روي عن كعب أنه قال : يجاء بالرجل يوم القيامة . فيوزن بالحبة فلا يزنها

MUQATIL:18:103-107/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r3.claim: They disbelieved God's signs, meaning the Quran, and the meeting in the Resurrection where deeds are repaid; their good deeds are void because they lacked faith.
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r3.anchor: { أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم } ، يعني القرآن، { ولقائه } ، يعني بالبعث الذي فيه جزاء الأعمال، { فحبطت أعمالهم } ،

MUQATIL:18:103-107/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r4.claim: Their deeds carry no weight on the Day of Resurrection, not even the equivalent of a mosquito's wing.
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r4.anchor: فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا } [آية: 105]، من خير قدر مثقال جناح بعوضة.

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.claim: The greatest losers are those who disbelieve in God’s signs and meeting Him, because their worldly efforts are futile.
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.anchor: Those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, and in the meeting with Him (v. 105) are described in this passage as the greatest losers

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r3.claim: Their deeds come to nothing because they disbelieve; deeds without faith are assigned no weight.
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r3.anchor: their deeds have come to naught, because they are disbelievers, and deeds without faith are assigned no weight

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r4.claim: Another verse compares the deeds of those who deny their prophets to scattered dust.
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r4.anchor: In 25:23, it is said that the deeds of those who are guilty of denying their prophets will be as scattered dust

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.claim: These six verses draw a conclusion from the sūrah’s account of worldly seduction, reliance on protectors besides God, spiritual blindness, and bad outcomes, and prepare for the closing declaration at 18:110.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات الست في منزلة الاستنتاج مما تقدم من آيات السورة

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.claim: The indirect address in “shall We inform you” targets polytheists, made explicit by the later description of those who disbelieved in God’s signs and meeting Him; the plural “deeds” stresses their varied losses.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن الخطاب للمشركين وهو مسوق سوق الكناية

TABRISI:18:99-105/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:99-105/r9.claim: They rejected God's proofs and the meeting with His recompense, so their works were null because they did them contrary to God's command.
TABRISI:18:99-105/r9.anchor: جحدوا بحجج الله وبيناته ولقاء جزائه في الآخرة

TABRISI:18:99-105/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:99-105/r10.claim: To say that God will assign them no weight means they have no value, rank, or honor with Him and will be disregarded and punished; Arabic usage treats weight as status and worth.
TABRISI:18:99-105/r10.anchor: أي لا قيمة لهم عندنا ولا كرامة ولا نعتد بهم

THALABI:v6p200#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p200#2/r5.claim: Those who disbelieve in God's signs and meeting Him have their deeds nullified and will have no weight on Judgment Day.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r5.anchor: فحبطت: بطلت وذهبت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا

THALABI:v6p200#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v6p200#2/r6.claim: He says some people bring deeds as great as the mountains of Tihama, yet they weigh nothing.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r6.anchor: يأتي أناس بأعمال يوم القيامة هي في العظم عندهم كجبال تهامة

THALABI:v6p200#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p200#2/r7.claim: The Prophet says a huge, heavy man may weigh less than a mosquito's wing on Judgment Day.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r7.anchor: يأتي الرجل العظيم السمين يوم القيامة فلا يزن جناح بعوضة

THALABI:v6p200#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r8.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
THALABI:v6p200#2/r8.claim: He says usury has seventy gates, the least like incest; the worst usury is insulting a Muslim, and a glutton may weigh less than a mosquito's wing.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r8.anchor: الربا سبعون بابا أهونهن مثل نكاح الرجل أمه

THALABI:v6p200#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r9.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
THALABI:v6p200#2/r9.claim: He calls slandering one's Muslim brother the worst form of usury.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r9.anchor: وأربى الربى عرض أخيك المسلم تشتمه

THALABI:v6p200#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r10.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
THALABI:v6p200#2/r10.claim: He gives the example of a tall, voracious man who weighs less than a mosquito's wing and recites the verse about no weight being assigned.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r10.anchor: ويؤتى يوم القيامة بالعظيم الطويل الأكول الشروب الذي يشرب الظرف

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r3.claim: Those who reject God's signs and meeting Him lose their deeds and receive no weight on Judgment Day; this parallels the light scales in another verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r3.anchor: فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا} [الكهف: 105] وهي مثل قوله: {ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون} [المؤمنون: 103]

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.claim: People direct their efforts toward their aims: seeking God’s pleasure and the afterlife leads to one kind of work, while pursuit of worldly gain leads to another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.anchor: İnsanlar, davranışlarında daima bir amaç gözetip ona göre çaba harcarlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.claim: Polytheists think their idols bring them nearer to God and that shirk is obedience, but God gives their deeds no value in this life or the next.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.anchor: Allah’a ortak koşanlar tanrılarının kendilerini Allah’a yaklaştıracağını ve Allah katında küfür sayılan bu davranışlarının Allah’a itaat olduğunu sanmaktadırlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r3.claim: The Prophet said that on Judgment Day many large, heavy men will weigh no more with God than a gnat’s wing, and cited the verse about worthless deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r3.anchor: Kıyamet gününde şişman ve iri cüsseli nice adamlar gelir ki Allah katında sivri sineğin kanadı kadar ağırlığı yoktur.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These verses humble people who thought themselves superior and mocked revelation: they will become insignificant and taste Hell as the consequence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Today they regard themselves to be superior but on the Day of Judgement they will become insignificant. They haughtily made fun of God’s revelations

BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r1.claim: The people in view are those previously described as misguided in effort while assuming they did well.
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r1.anchor: المنعوتون بما ذكر من ضلال السعي مع الحسبان المزبور

BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r2.claim: They disbelieve God’s rational and transmitted signs of oneness and deny the resurrection and afterlife.
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r2.anchor: كفروا باايات} بدلائله الداعية إلى التوحيد عقلا ونقلا {ولقآااه} بالبعث

BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r3.claim: Their deeds are entirely nullified by unbelief, so they receive no reward.
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r3.anchor: {فحبطت} بطلت بذلك {أعمالهم} المعهودة حبوطا كليا فلا يثابون عليها

BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r4.claim: Not weighing them means despising them and assigning them no value because their good works have been erased.
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r4.anchor: حبوط الأعمال {وزنا} أي : فنزدري بهم ولا نجعل لهم مقدارا واعتبارا

BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r5.claim: A report describes a tall, gluttonous drinker as weighing less than a mosquito’s wing because of his worthlessness and unbelief; the scale is not set for unbelievers whose good works are erased.
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r5.anchor: يؤتى بالرجل الطويل الأكول الشروب فلا يزن جناح بعوضة

BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r6.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation says a person’s and deeds’ weight depends on sincerity: without it neither has value, as 25:23 likens such works to scattered dust.
BURSEVI:v5p234#2/r6.anchor: لأن وزن الأشخاص والأعمال في ميزان القيامة إنما يكون بحسب الصدق والإخلاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r1.claim: The demonstrative sharply identifies the described people and signals that their traits make them fit the ensuing judgment, as in 2:5.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r1.anchor: وجيء باسم الإشارة لتمييزهم أكمل تمييز لئلا يلتبسوا بغيرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r2.claim: Here آيات means the Quran and miracles, while حبط means becoming void and being refuted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r2.anchor: والآيات : القرآن والمعجزات . والحبط : البطلان والدحض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r3.claim: Depending on the earlier readings of هل ننبئكم, ربهم is either an overt noun where a pronoun was expected or the expected wording; the following نون is either ordinary or a shift from ربهم.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r4.claim: Not establishing a weight means disregarding them as insignificant things are not weighed; the verse depicts them as contemptible through a sustained metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r4.anchor: لأن الناس يزنون الأشياء المتنافس في مقاديرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r5.claim: Their deeds being annulled explains their lack of weight: with no good works left, they count for nothing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p47/r5.anchor: وجعل عدم إقامة الوزن مفرعا على حبط أعمالهم لأنهم بحبط أعمالهم صاروا محقرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r1.claim: The description first concerns Arab disbelievers who rejected resurrection; ḥabiṭat means their deeds became void, including whatever good they had done.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r2.claim: One literal reading is that no good deeds remain to place on their scales; a person with no good deeds must be in Hell.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r3.claim: Alternatively, the weighing language is metaphorical and means they have no standing or worth with God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's comparison of a gluttonous, long-bodied man who weighs less than a mosquito, after which he recited this verse.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r5.claim: Saʿd identifies the people who lose their worldly effort while thinking it good as worshippers among Jews and Christians, including monks and hermits.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r6.claim: Ali identifies the group as the Khawarij; a report says he told Ibn al-Kawwa that he and his companions were the greatest losers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r7.claim: The author weakens these sectarian identifications because the following verses describe people who disbelieved in the meeting with God, unlike Jews, Christians, or Khawarij as groups.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r7.anchor: ويضعف هذا كله قوله تعالى بعد ذلك أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه وليس من هذه الطوائف من يكفر بلقاء الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r8.claim: He takes the passage as describing polytheistic idol-worshippers; Saʿd and Ali may have named only groups exemplifying part of the opening description.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r8.anchor: فاتجه بهذا ما قلناه أولا وعلي وسعد رضي الله عنهما ذكرا أقواما أخذوا بحظهم من صدر الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r9.claim: Aʿmālan is accusative as a specification (tamyīz).

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r10.claim: They read fa-ḥabiṭat with fatḥa on the bāʾ, whereas the majority use kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «فحبطت» بكسر الباء، وقرأ ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r11.claim: Mujahid reads fa-lā yuqīm with yāʾ, meaning God does not set up their weight; the majority use the first-person plural nūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r11.anchor: وقرأ كعب بن عجرة والحسن وأبو عمرو ونافع والناس «فلا نقيم لهم» بنون العظمة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r12.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r12.claim: He reads fa-lā yaqūm, making the weighing a nominative subject; Mujahid also reports a yāʾ reading of yaqūlu lahum.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r12.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير: «فلا يقوم» ويلزمه أن يقرأ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p545/r13.claim: Dhālika points to the abandonment of weighing; their recompense is the predicate, with Hell as an appositive, while mā in bimā kafarū is verbal and huzʾ means mockery.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r1.claim: They denied the signs of God’s oneness and denied resurrection and recompense; their rejection of the Messenger and Qurʾan entails those denials, so their efforts are void for lack of faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r1.anchor: جحدوا دلائل توحيده وكفروا بالبعث والجزاء وذلك أنهم بكفرهم برسول الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Jahdari read “we do not establish” with a masculine yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والجحدري فلا يقيم بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r3.claim: One interpretation says only obedience weighs in the balance, and an unbeliever has no obedience to weigh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r3.anchor: إنما يثقل الميزان بالطاعة وإنما توزن الحسنات والسيئات والكافر لا طاعة له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r4.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says “no weight” means no worth or rank; a Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says a tall, gluttonous drinker will not weigh a mosquito’s wing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي في تفسير هذه الآية يقال ما لفلان عندنا وزن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari gives a third interpretation: the scales are not established in their favor, because they weigh against them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#4/r5.anchor: فلا نقيم لهم لأن الوزن عليهم لا لهم ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r1.claim: These people denied God's worldly signs and proofs of His oneness and the truth of His messengers, and rejected the Hereafter; their works are void and their scales empty of good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r1.anchor: لا نثقل موازينهم؛ لأنها خالية عن الخير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r2.claim: The Prophet says a huge, heavy man will weigh no more with God than a mosquito's wing, and recites this verse; al-Bukhārī includes it and Muslim transmits a second route.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r3.claim: Another report says an enormous eater and drinker will not outweigh a seed; it is transmitted by Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Jarīr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r3.anchor: يؤتى بالرجل الأكول الشروب العظيم، فيوزن بحبة فلا يزنها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r4.speaker: بريدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r4.claim: A report describes a Qurashī man strutting in fine clothes whom God will assign no weight on Resurrection; al-Bazzār notes its narrators Wāṣil and ʿAwn are weak and unsupported.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r4.anchor: هذا ممن لا يقيم الله له يوم القيامة وزنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r5.speaker: كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r5.claim: Kaʿb says a huge, tall man will be brought on Resurrection and weigh less than a mosquito's wing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p202/r5.anchor: يؤتى يوم القيامة برجل عظيم طويل، فلا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r1.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī identifies those whose efforts were lost as monks, compared with those who toil in 88:3.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r1.anchor: ضل سعيهم } ضاع وبطل وهم الرهبان . عن علي رضي الله عنه ، كقوله : { عاملة ناصبة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says they are the People of the Book.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r3.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r3.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwāʾ who they were, ʿAlī said some were the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r3.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : أن ابن الكوا سأله عنهم ؟ فقال : منهم أهل حروراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r4.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports people bringing deeds they thought immense as Tihāma’s mountains, yet weighing nothing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r4.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري : يأتي ناس بأعمال يوم القيامة هي عندهم في العظم كجبال تهامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r5.claim: God assigns them no weight or worth; alternatively no scales are erected for them, because scales are reserved for monotheists with good and bad deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r5.anchor: فنزدري بهم ولا يكون لهم عندنا وزن ومقدار . وقيل : لا يقام لهم ميزان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r6.claim: A reading has the verb in third-person masculine: fa-lā yuqīmu.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r7.claim: ‘Those whose efforts were lost’ may be nominative as an answer, accusative as censure, or genitive as apposition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p699#2/r7.anchor: الأوجه أن يكون في محل الرفع ، على : هم الذين ضل سعيهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#6/r1.claim: The disbelievers' deeds are nullified and they will have no weight or worth before God on Judgment Day.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا ﴾ فلا يكون لهم عندنا وزن ومقدار

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r2.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r2.claim: The majority read ḥabiṭat with kasra on the bāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reads ḥabiṭat with fatḥa on the bāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r4.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r4.claim: The majority read nuqīmu with the majestic plural nūn.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r5.claim: Mujahid reads yuqīmu in the third person, meaning that God does not establish a weight for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r5.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد بياء الغائب يريد فلا يقيم الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r6.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r6.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads fa-lā yaqūmu lahum yawma al-qiyāmati wazn, and says even an enormous eater and drinker may weigh no more than a mosquito's wing before God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r6.anchor: فلا يقوم لهم يوم القيامة وزن

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says ʿUbayd's statement is not personal opinion; a sound report in Bukhari and Muslim from Abū Hurayra confirms that a huge, heavy man may weigh no more than a mosquito's wing.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r7.anchor: لا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة اقرءوا إن شئتم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r8.claim: The verse means the unbelievers have no reward or good deeds to place on the scales; their deeds face punishment, and one with no good deed is in Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r8.anchor: والمعنى أنهم لا ثواب لهم، وأعمالهم مقابلة بالعذاب،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r9.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says deeds as great as the mountains of Tihāma may weigh nothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r9.anchor: يؤتى بأعمال كجبال تهامة فلا تزن شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes the weighing as metaphor: they will have no standing or worth before God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r10.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن يريد المجاز والاستعارة كأنه قال: فلا قدر لهم عندنا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r11.claim: The reports condemn deliberately acquired obesity caused by overeating and luxury; they indicate excess beyond sufficiency for indulgence and weight gain is forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r11.anchor: بل يدل على تحريم الأكل الزائد على قدر الكفاية

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r12.claim: A prophetic report calls the corpulent religious scholar the most hated of men to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r12.anchor: إن أبغض الرجال إلى الله تعالى الحبر السمين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r13.speaker: عمران بن حصين
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r13.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reports the Prophet's warning about later people who testify without being asked, betray trust, vow without fulfillment, and become corpulent.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r14.claim: Acquired corpulence stems from gluttony, ease, and unchecked desire, making a person serve the self rather than God and prone to unlawful conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r14.anchor: فهو عبد نفسه لا عبد ربه

SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r1.claim: He reads فحبطت with a fatḥa on ب.
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس " فحبطت " بفتح الباء

SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r2.claim: The common reading نقيم uses the first-person plural from أقام; Mujahid and Ubayd ibn Umayr read يقيم with a third-person pronoun returning to آيات ربهم.
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r2.anchor: والعامة على " نقيم " بنون العظمة من " أقام ". ومجاهد وعبيد بن عمير. " فلا يقيم " بياء الغيبة

SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r3.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r3.claim: Mujahid also reads فلا يقوم لهم with قام and raises وزن as its subject.
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r3.anchor: ومجاهد أيضا " فلا يقوم لهم " مضارع قام، " وزن " بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r4.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r4.claim: He also reads فلا يقوم وزنا in the accusative, apparently assuming قام is transitive; the author prefers taking their deeds or efforts as subject, with وزن circumstantial or specification.
SAMIN-DURR:18:105/r4.anchor: وعن عبيد بن عمير أيضا " فلا يقوم وزنا " بالنصب كأنه توهم أن " قام " متعد

RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r1.claim: Meeting God can mean seeing Him: although liqāʾ originally means arrival or encounter, its familiar metaphorical use for seeing is preferable to inserting an unstated phrase meaning meeting His reward.
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r1.anchor: حمل اللفظ على المجاز المتعارف المشهور أولى من حمله على ما يحتاج معه إلى الإضمار

RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila infer from deeds being nullified that the doctrines of abatement and expiation are true; al-Razi refers the detailed discussion to al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r2.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بقوله تعالى : { فحبطت أعمالهم } على أن القول بالإحباط والتكفير حق

RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r3.claim: One interpretation of having no weight is that God will disdain them and they will have no worth.
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r3.anchor: الأول : أنا نزدري بهم وليس لهم عندنا وزن ومقدار

RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that no scales are set for them: scales distinguish good and bad deeds among monotheists.
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r4.anchor: لا نقيم لهم ميزانا لأن الميزان إنما يوضع لأهل الحسنات والسيئات من الموحدين

RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r5.claim: The Qadi says that when sins outweigh a person’s good deeds, the obedience counts as though it never existed, so none of it enters the weighing; this relies on abatement.
RAZI-FULL:v21p148/r5.anchor: الثالث : قال القاضي : إن من غلبت معاصيه صار ما في فعله من الطاعة كأن لم يكن

TABATABAI:18:105-107/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r2.claim: The losers are those who deny God's signs in the world and themselves, as well as the signs and miracles brought by prophets; denying encounter with God means rejecting return to Him and resurrection, a trait of idolaters.
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r2.anchor: آياته تعالى في الآفاق والأنفس وما يأتي به الأنبياء والرسل من المعجزات

TABATABAI:18:105-107/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r3.claim: Their deeds are void because they neither act for God nor seek the next life's reward and happiness, and remembrance of Judgment does not motivate them.
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r3.anchor: أنهم لا يعملون عملا لوجه الله ولا يريدون ثواب الدار الآخرة

TABATABAI:18:105-107/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r4.claim: The weighing of deeds at Judgment measures the heaviness of good deeds; because these people's deeds are null, they have no weight, as shown by the cited passage.
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r4.anchor: والوزن يوم القيامة بثقل الحسنات على ما يدل عليه قوله تعالى

ASAD-NOTES:18:103#n104/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:103#n104/r1.speaker: Al-Qadi ‘Iyad
ASAD-NOTES:18:103#n104/r1.claim: Al-Qadi ‘Iyad, quoted by Razi, says sinners’ good deeds count on Judgment Day but are outweighed by their godlessness.
ASAD-NOTES:18:103#n104/r1.anchor: whatever good such sinners may do is far outweighed by their godlessness (Al-Qadi 'Iyad, as quoted by Razi)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r1.claim: The most lost are those who reject God’s signs, the evidence of His oneness and power, and the meeting of resurrection, reward, and punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r1.anchor: جحدوا دلائل توحيده وقدرته {ولقائه} وكفروا بالبعث، والثواب، والعقاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r2.claim: Their deeds came to nothing: their striving was nullified.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون عن أبي هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says a huge, tall, gluttonous man will weigh less than a mosquito’s wing, then cites this verse; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r3.anchor: ليؤتين يوم القيامة بالعظيم، الطويل، الشروب، الأكلول فلا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r4.speaker: كعب بن عجرة؛ عبيد بن عمير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r4.claim: They report a man weighed against a grain and then a mosquito’s wing without weighing even that much, and recite the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r4.anchor: يؤتى برجل يوم القيامة فيوزن بحبة فلا يزنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r5.claim: They have no weight because only someone with righteous deeds and monotheistic faith is weighed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r5.anchor: إنما يوزن من له عمل صالح، وكان على التوحيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r6.speaker: author؛ أبو العباس عن ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r6.claim: The reports seem to weigh the men themselves, but the author rejects that reading: deeds are weighed, and “has no weight” idiomatically means having no worth or standing with God; even the enormous glutton in the hadith lacks value without monotheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r6.anchor: والصحيح في هذا ما قاله أهل المعاني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r7.claim: Another explanation is that the unbelievers’ scales are light in good deeds because they lack the monotheism that makes the scales heavy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r8.claim: The apparent weighing of unbelievers can be retained as a humiliation, showing all creatures that they weigh less than an atom or mosquito’s wing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165#2/r8.anchor: يأمر بوزن أهل الكفر تحقيرا لهم، وتصغيرا لأمرهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:105/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:105/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:105/r1.claim: They disbelieved God’s signs of oneness, including the Quran, and meeting Him, meaning resurrection; their efforts are null, and God humiliates them in the Fire without regard.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r1.claim: The opening is a new divine statement completing the description of the greatest losers and specifying its referents; it is not included within the preceding command.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r1.anchor: كلام مستأنف من جنابه تعالى مسوق لتكميل تعريف الأخسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r2.claim: The rejected signs are God's proofs calling to monotheism, both transmitted and rational; another view limits them to the Quran, but the author prefers the broader reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r2.anchor: بدلائله سبحانه الداعية إلى التوحيد الشاملة للسمعية والعقلية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r3.claim: Most commentators take meeting God as a metonym for resurrection, gathering, and subsequent afterlife events; the literal meeting is not intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r3.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه كناية عن البعث والحشر وما يتبع ذلك من أمور الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r4.claim: The alternative interpretation supplies an omitted word to mean meeting God's punishment, which the author deems unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r4.anchor: أي لقاء عذابه تعالى وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Sammal read the bāʾ in faḥabiṭat with fatḥa rather than the usual kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو السمال بفتحها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r6.claim: The fāʾ marks the consequence of disbelief in God's signs and meeting Him, and the deeds in question are wholly nullified.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r6.anchor: أي فحبطت لذلك ( أعمالهم ( المعهودة حبوطا كليا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r7.claim: The denial of weight means God will disdain and disregard them, since care and esteem depend on righteous works that have been entirely nullified.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r7.anchor: فنزدري بهم ونحتقرهم ولا نجعل لهم مقدارا واعتبارا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r8.claim: Alternatively, no scales are set for their deeds because the deeds became dust; the author prefers the first interpretation because the second merely repeats their nullification.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r8.anchor: أو لا نضع لأجل وزن أعمالهم ميزانا لأنها قد حبطت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r9.claim: The preferred reading is not a Mu'tazilite position; the objection that contempt arises from disbelief rather than nullification is, the author says, caused by heedlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r9.anchor: وليس من الاعتزال في شيء وقرأ مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r10.claim: Mujahid and Ubayd ibn Umayr read the verb as third-person singular, because God's signs are mentioned immediately before it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وعبيد بن عمير ( فلا يقيم ) بالياء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r11.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r11.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr also has a reading with fatḥa on the imperfect prefix, treating qāma as transitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r11.anchor: وعند عبيد أيضا ( فلا يقيم ) بفتح ياء المضارعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r12.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin, and Yaqub also read an intransitive verb, with weight as its subject: no weight stands for them on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p48/r12.anchor: وعن مجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب بخلاف عنهم ( فلا يقوم لهم يوم القيامة وزن )

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r1.claim: God's signs mean the Quran or proofs establishing unity and prophethood; meeting Him means resurrection or encountering His punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r1.anchor: بالقرآن أو بدلائله المنصوبة على التوحيد والنبوة. { ولقائه } بالبعث على ما هو عليه أو لقاء عذابه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r2.claim: Their deeds are void through disbelief, so they receive no reward; not weighing them means either despising them or setting up no scale because their works are void.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:105/r2.anchor: بكفرهم فلا يثابون عليها. { فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيمة وزنا } فنزدري بهم ولا نجعل لهم مقدارا

DURR-FULL:v5p466/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r2.speaker: راوٍ غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r2.claim: For the unbeliever, his deeds appear in a hideous, foul form; he recognizes them, rides them to God, and is given no weight.
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r2.anchor: وإذا كان كافرا مثل له عمله في أقبح صورة رآها وأنتنه فكلما جاءه روع

DURR-FULL:v5p466/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r3.speaker: عمير
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r3.claim: A physically imposing, tall man can weigh less than a mosquito's wing before God, as the verse says.
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r3.anchor: عن عمير قال: يؤتى بالرجل العظيم الطويل يوم القيامة فيوضع في الميزان فلا يزن

DURR-FULL:v5p466/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r4.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r4.claim: A man may weigh less than a grain of wheat, barley, or even a mosquito's wing; thus the unbelievers have no weight.
DURR-FULL:v5p466/r4.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة في قوله: {فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا}

JISHUMI:v6p4506/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r5.claim: The statement that deeds are nullified supports the doctrine that deeds can cancel one another.
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: فحبطت أعمالهم على تحابط الأعمال

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r1.claim: Abduh argues that shifts in rhyme and cadence within a surah can heighten beauty and emotional force, renew the reader’s attention, and sharpen the listener’s ear.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r1.anchor: ومن اللطائف البديعة التي يخالف بها نظم القرآن كلام العرب من شعر أو نثر، أنك ترى السور ذات النظم الخاص والقوافي المقفاة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r2.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r2.claim: Abduh answers that rhetorical taste is not unknowable: people who dismiss it lack command of eloquent Arabic, which is acquired by studying and using its best speech.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r2.anchor: ويتصدّى الشيخ محمد عبده لمن يمارون في مثل هذا الكلام عن البلاغة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r3.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r3.claim: Abduh favors early works, especially Asrar al-Balagha and Dalail al-Ijaz, because they connect rhetorical principles to felt responses rather than late technical rules.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p131/r3.anchor: وبخاصة (أسرار البلاغة، ودلائل الإعجاز) لأنهما الكتابان اللذان يحيلانك في قوانين البلاغة على وجدانك وجنانك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati, following the cited argument, says rhetorical rules are derived from eloquent speech; they cannot substitute for reading, memorizing, and understanding it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r1.anchor: والقوانين الموضوعة لها مستنبطة من الكلام البليغ وليس هو مستبطاً منها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r2.claim: To judge the Quran’s eloquence requires a cultivated command of Arabic poetry and prose; its historical effect on Arabs and skilled non-Arabs is evidence, and eloquence reaches both reason and feeling.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p132/r2.anchor: فمعرفة مكان القرآن من البلاغة لا يحكمها من الجهة الفنية والذوقية إلا من أوتي حظاً عظيماً من مختار كلام البلغاء المنظوم والمنثور

ITQAN:v3p166/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p166/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p166/r11.claim: The verse omits an adjective after وزنا: the intended weight is one of benefit.
ITQAN:v3p166/r11.anchor: ﴿ فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا ﴾ أي نافعا
